Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Iris, 10:10: works for me. the list needs a clear label, though. “Extra: the glass buoy” is more obvious than “Case 6,” especially for visitors who start listening halfway through and aren't following the printed map.

Dev, 10:14: let's use “Extra: the glass buoy.” i can change the player menu, but the printed map is already at the printer. they're doing 120 copies this afternoon, so that label won't make this batch.

Maya, 10:19: right, no point holding the maps for one optional track. i'll add a small note to the front desk sheet so staff can point it out if someone asks where the buoy audio is.

Noor, 10:23: another small thing: the audio starts automatically when you scan the blue symbol, but it takes a second or two to load in the back corner. we should tell the floor team not to scan it twice while they're waiting.

Iris, 10:28: yes, i saw that too. if you scan again it queues the same track twice, and then the second one starts after the first ends. Sal said the load delay is normal on the older players, not a broken tag.

Dev, 10:33: i'll put that in the staff note, along with the volume reset. the players come back at 60 percent after charging, even if someone turned one down earlier. we have six units ready and two still with the tech desk.

Maya, 10:38: thanks. for the walkthrough, can we use units 2 through 7 and leave the two from the tech desk out? one has a loose headphone jack, and the other keeps restarting when the screen sleeps.

Noor, 10:42: yep, those six are all charged. i'll put a green dot on the ready units and leave the faulty ones in the locked drawer, so they don't get picked up by the school group before the repair is done.

Iris, 10:46: i'll bring the large-print route sheet too. it's two pages now, not one, because the type is 18 point; that should be easier to follow at the bench. the revised copies are in the education office.

Dev, 10:50: perfect. i'll add the new route timing to the walkthrough sheet: about 14 minutes without the buoy track, and 16 with it. those numbers came from the staff test, not the visitor session.

Maya, 10:55: one last thing, the west doorway sign says the closure ends at noon, so please don't route anyone through there during the morning test even if the barrier is moved early. facilities said they still need to check the floor edge.

Noor, 11:01: understood. i'll meet the school group at the ticket desk at 11:15 and ask them to wait by the bench until the rope line is set. the teacher said there'll be 18 students and two adults.
